text: The line graph illustrates how many minutes per day people in three age groups spent on social media between 2012 and 2022.

Overall, time spent on social media rose in all three age groups, with the youngest group consistently spending the most, although growth slowed markedly in the final years. The oldest group, however, showed the lowest figures throughout.

Those aged 16–24 spent 60 minutes a day on social media in 2012, and this figure more than doubled to 150 minutes by 2020, before levelling off at 155 minutes in 2022. The sharpest increase for this group came between 2012 and 2018, when daily use rose by 75 minutes. Usage in all groups was highest in 2022.

The 25–44 group followed a similar but lower pattern, climbing from 35 to 98 minutes, while the oldest group started at only 15 minutes and reached 45 minutes in 2022. Although the gap between the youngest and oldest groups widened in absolute terms, from 45 minutes to 110 minutes, the oldest group tripled its usage, which was the largest proportional rise.
